part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `digit_grouping::write_grouped_int` (include/fmt/format.h:3229), which is used for all localized (`{:L}`) integer formatting via `write_loc` → `format_facet` / the wide-char `write_loc` in xchar.h:25. It unconditionally rendered decimal digits (`render_digits_for_specs` always called `render_decimal_digits`) and emitted only a single sign character as prefix, so `{:LX}` produced `123456789` instead of `75BCD15`.

The rewrite:
- renders digits in the base requested by the presentation type (`d`/none → decimal, `x`/`X` → hex with case, `b`/`B` → binary, `o` → octal, `c` → char, invalid → format error), matching the non-grouped `write_int` behavior
- applies alternate-form prefixes (`0x`, `0X`, `0b`, `0B`, and `0` for octal per the same rules as `write_int`) on top of the sign prefix, writing all prefix bytes before the grouped digits
- computes the padded size as prefix chars + digits + thousands separators, keeping digit grouping (e.g. `7,5bc,d15`) for any base

Verified: all 20 test suites pass (`ctest` in the container), including the previously failing `format_test.format_locale` (`{:Lx}`, `{:#Lb}`, `{:10Lo}`), locale tests in `xchar-test`, `group_digits_view`, `format_facet*`, and both compiled and header-only builds produce correct results for the original repro and edge cases (width, alignment, sign, alt forms, wide strings).
